            bool ansi_is_already_colorized (const char * message, size_t
            pos)
          

          

            #include <include/ascii-chat/video/terminal/ansi.h>
          

          

            Check if a position in text is already colored. Scans from the start
            of the message to the given position, tracking ANSI escape codes.
            Returns true if there is an active color code (not in reset state).
          

          

          
Detects reset codes: \x1b[0m and \x1b[m

          

          
Parameters

          

            message The full message
            

            pos Position to check
          

          
Returns

          

            true if already colored (not in reset state), false if in reset
            state
          

          
Definition at line 102 of file ansi.c.

          
102                                                                 {
103   if (!message) {
104     return false;
105   }
106
107   bool in_reset = true; // Start in reset state
108
109   // Scan from beginning to current position looking for ANSI codes
110   for (size_t i = 0; i < pos && message[i] != '\0'; i++) {
111     if (message[i] == '\x1b' && message[i + 1] == '[') {
112       // Found ANSI escape sequence start
113       // Look for the end marker 'm'
114       size_t j = i + 2;
115       while (message[j] != '\0' && message[j] != 'm') {
116         j++;
117       }
118
119       if (message[j] == 'm') {
120         // Extract the color code part (between [ and m)
121         // Check if it's a reset code: \x1b[0m or \x1b[m
122         in_reset = ((j == i + 3 && message[i + 2] == '0') || (j == i + 2));
123       }
124     }
125   }
126
127   // Return true if NOT in reset state (already colorized)
128   return !in_reset;
129 }

            char * ansi_strip_escapes (const char * input, size_t
              input_len)
          

          

            #include <include/ascii-chat/video/terminal/ansi.h>
          

          

            Strip all ANSI escape sequences from a string. Removes all ANSI CSI
            sequences (ESC [ ... final_byte) from the input, leaving only
            printable text. Useful for creating plain text output from colorized
            ASCII art.
          

          

          
Parameters

          

            input Input string containing ANSI escape sequences
            

            input_len Length of input string
          

          
Returns

          

            Newly allocated string with escapes removed (caller must free), or
            NULL on error

33   char *output = SAFE_MALLOC(input_len + 1, char *);
34   if (!output) {
35     return NULL;
36   }

48       while (i < input_len) {

51         // Intermediate bytes: 0x20-0x2F (space, !, ", etc.)

61         char final = input[i];
62         if (final >= 0x40 && final <= 0x7E) {
63           i++;
64         }
65       }

67       // Regular character - copy to output
68       output[out_pos++] = input[i];
69       i++;
